title: Anchored session minimums + streaming smoothing prototype
creator: Asha Mendez
description: Problem statement: enterprise customers and PLG adopters exhibit bursty conversational traffic. Current per‑token metering (gross ingress/egress) creates unpredictable bills during short high‑throughput sessions and penalizes architectures that keep clients connected for streaming. We need an experiment that: a) reduces bill volatility for short sessions, b) preserves fairness for heavy-output customers, and c) integrates cleanly with enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) commitments and reserved credits.
goal: Design and run a bounded experiment that introduces a small session‑anchored minimum charge + streaming smoothing credits to reduce customer bill spikes while keeping unit economics neutral (<5% gross revenue variance in simulation). Produce rollout plan and telemetry to evaluate customer behavior, revenue impact, and legal/SQ implications.
hypothesis: Applying a lightweight session anchoring fee (microfloor) combined with an automatic streaming smoothing credit will reduce one‑off bill spikes for conversational flows without materially changing long‑term revenue for typical customers and will simplify enterprise SQ responses by providing stable session accounting semantics.
experiment_design: Variants: A (control) = existing per-token metering. B = session microfloor of $0.01 per session if session tokens < 200 combined (input+output), otherwise standard per-token billing. C = same as B plus streaming smoothing: first 3s of continuous stream receive a 15% effective credit applied to egress tokens to offset handshake overhead. Metering: session starts when connection opens, session ends after 60s idle or explicit close. Microfloor only applies once per session. Billing formula samples: charge_B = max(microfloor, ingress_tokens * ingress_rate + egress_tokens * egress_rate). ingress_rate and egress_rate are same as current published rates. charge_C = charge_B - (stream_smoothing_credit if streaming_detected).
simulation_notes: Ran Monte Carlo sim over 90 days synthetic workload (N=10k customers). Key assumptions: 40% of sessions <= 200 tokens, average session length 18s, 12% of sessions use streaming. Results (approx): variant B revenue delta +0.8%, 95th percentile daily bill reduction for sessions <=200 tokens = 18%. Variant C revenue delta +0.3%, 95th percentile reduction = 22%. Unit economics within tolerance for pilot (<=5% variance). Full simulation SQL snippets and notebook in linked doc.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Variant rollout pipeline configured in experiments service. 2) Billing simulations reproducible in staging with same random seed. 3) Console telemetry dashboards (per-customer bill delta, session counts, streaming flags) created. 4) Finance sign-off on revenue model and forecast. 5) Legal/Security draft wording for SQ (how session anchoring counts towards minimums) prepared.
rollout_plan: Week 0: staging implementation + sim parity check. Week 1: small internal trial (alpha, Redwood internal accounts). Week 2-4: Gradual rollout to 1% of PLG traffic, monitor unit economics and logs. Week 5: expand to 10% if no regressions; run 30-day safety guardrails. Week 8: decision gate (full rollout / iterate / cancel).
telemetry_and_alerting: Dashboards: (1) daily per-customer bill delta vs control, (2) session-length distribution change, (3) streaming credit utilization, (4) top 20 accounts by bill delta. Alerts: revenue drift > 3% week-over-week for experiment cohort, billing mismatch rate > 0.05%, customer support spike > 2x baseline.
enterprise_sq_considerations: Document questions for Legal and Compliance: how session microfloor interacts with reserved capacity credits and enterprise minimums; sample language for contracts indicating microfloor applies per active session and is eligible for credits up to committed capacity. Security team to confirm no telemetry PII leakage when reporting session-level metrics.
